summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following his second transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure targeting residual tumors in liver segments VI/VII and VIII. The procedure was performed successfully via the right femoral artery, delivering doxorubicin-eluting beads to the tumor bed. Access to a suspected phrenic artery supply was attempted but not achieved due to contrast and radiation limits. The patient remained stable throughout, with no post-procedural pain, nausea, or fever. Liver enzymes rose mildly as expected, and blood counts showed a transient decline. He was discharged home on day two with instructions to monitor for post-embolization syndrome, continue all home medications—including nadolol, spironolactone, glyburide, aspirin, and pravastatin—and follow up with oncology and hepatology in four weeks for imaging and treatment assessment.
